lesson.title: Départ, Arrivée & Aller-Retour
lesson.subtitle: Combining aller, partir, arriver, and prendre for real travel scenarios.

hook.title: Departures, Arrivals & Round-Trip Tickets: Aller simple vs. Aller-retour
hook.content: At the ticket counter, aller ('going', used as a noun) + simple ('single') = 'a one-way ticket' (un aller simple), and aller + retour ('going-return') = 'a round-trip / return ticket' (un aller-retour)! And ticket destinations take pour ('for'): un aller-retour pour Lyon!

footnotes.title: How French turns the infinitive 'aller' into a masculine noun ('un aller')
footnotes.content: French uses the infinitive aller as a masculine noun meaning 'the outbound journey': un aller simple, un aller-retour!

pattern.title: un aller simple (One-Way) vs. un aller-retour (Round-Trip)
pattern.content: Combine ticket buying with departure and arrival times.
pattern.linguist_note: Nominalized infinitives (l'aller, le dîner, le déjeuner) are always masculine in French.
pattern.trap_note: When buying a ticket 'to Lyon', French uses pour ('for Lyon'): un billet pour Lyon!

exercises.prompt: Match each travel expression with its English meaning:

matching_pairs.english: un billet pour Lyon (pour = 'to' on tickets!)

exercises.target_answer: a one-way / single ticket, a round-trip / return ticket, a ticket to Lyon, the departure / the arrival, I am coming back tomorrow
exercises.meaning: un aller simple, un aller-retour, un billet pour Lyon (pour = 'to' on tickets!), le départ / l'arrivée, Je reviens demain (revenir)
exercises.explanation: Ticket destinations take pour: un aller-retour pour Paris.

exercises.prompt: What is the literal word-for-word meaning of 'un aller-retour pour Paris'?
exercises.meaning: Literal structure: a go-return for Paris

exercises.prompt: How do you ask the ticket agent for 'a round-trip ticket to Lyon, please'?
options: Je voudrais un aller-retour pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît
Je voudrais un aller simple à Lyon, s'il vous plaît
exercises.target_answer: Je voudrais un aller-retour pour Lyon, s'il vous plaît
exercises.meaning: I would like a round-trip ticket to Lyon, please

exercises.idea: the train leaves this morning and I am coming back tomorrow (use Le train part ce matin)
cues: The train leaves this morning → Le train part ce matin
and I come back tomorrow → et je reviens demain
idea_parts: departure → Le train part ce matin
exercises.target_answer: Le train part ce matin et je reviens demain
exercises.meaning: The train leaves this morning and I'm coming back tomorrow
exercises.explanation: part is the 3rd-person singular of partir; je reviens is from revenir.

diagnosis.cue: Conjugate Le train part and je reviens.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: J'ai pris un aller-retour pour Marseille
exercises.target_answer: J'ai pris un aller-retour pour Marseille
exercises.meaning: I got a round-trip ticket to Marseille
exercises.affirmation: You wrote un aller-retour with its hyphen cleanly.

summary.outcome: Buy one-way (aller simple) and round-trip (aller-retour) tickets with pour + city, and state departure and return plans.

use_example.german: Un aller-retour pour Bordeaux, s'il vous plaît.
use_example.english: A round-trip ticket to Bordeaux, please.

summary.takeaway: One-way = un aller simple; Round-trip = un aller-retour; Ticket destination = pour [City].
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on Le Pont ([5141] Docteur, Professeur & Acteur): see how Départ, Arrivée & Aller-Retour leads directly into Docteur, Professeur & Acteur.

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "The train leaves this morning and I'm coming back tomorrow" in French:
twist.target_answer: Le train part ce matin et je reviens demain
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Le train part ce matin et je reviens demain" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Départ, Arrivée & Aller-Retour.

aller.context_translation: I'm going to go to the café.
aller.etymology_derivation: Latin ambulāre 'to walk' → ambler → aller. To go is a stroll away — and the near future rides on it.

arriver.context_translation: The train is going to arrive.

parti.etymology_derivation: partir takes être in the past: je suis parti(e).

revenir.context_translation: I'm going to come back tomorrow.

train.context_phrase: Le train part à huit heures.
train.etymology_derivation: Old French traïn 'a line of things pulled along'.

gare.etymology_derivation: Originally a river shelter where boats pulled in.

billet.etymology_derivation: Double ll after i sounds like /j/.

demain.context_translation: Tomorrow, I'm going to visit Lyon.
